questions.text: Consider  a  computer  with  a  4  MHz  processor.  Its  DMA  controller  can  transfer 8 bytes in 1 cycle from a device to main memory through cycle stealing at regular intervals. Which one of the following is the data transfer rate (in bits per second) of the DMA controller if 1% of the processor cycles are used for DMA?
questions.solution:
Cycles used by DMA per second [latex]=1\%\times4\times10^6=4\times10^4[/latex].
Each cycle moves 8 bytes = 64 bits.

Rate [latex]=4\times10^4\times64=2.56\times10^6[/latex] bits/s = 25,60,000 bps

Answer: 25,60,000

questions.text:
Let [latex] p [/latex] and [latex] q [/latex] be the following propositions:

[latex] p [/latex] : Fail grade can be given.
[latex] q [/latex] : Student scores more than [latex] 50 \% [/latex] marks.

Consider the statement: "Fail grade cannot be given when student scores more than [latex] 50 \% [/latex] marks."
Which one of the following is the CORRECT representation of the above statement in propositional logic?
questions.solution:
"Fail grade cannot be given when student scores more than 50%" means: if [latex]q[/latex] (scores [latex]\gt[/latex] 50%) then not [latex]p[/latex] (fail cannot be given).

[latex]q\rightarrow\neg p[/latex]

Answer: [latex]q\rightarrow\neg p[/latex]

questions.text:
The format of a single-precision floating-point number as per the IEEE 754 standard is:

Choose the largest floating-point number among the following options.
questions.solution:
In IEEE 754, an exponent of all 1s (255) is reserved for [latex]\infty[/latex]/NaN.

- (A): exponent 127 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]1.11\ldots1\times2^{0}\approx2[/latex]
- (B): exponent [latex]11111110=254[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]1.11\ldots1\times2^{127}\approx2^{128}[/latex], the largest finite number
- (C): exponent 255 with non-zero mantissa [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] NaN, not a number at all
- (D): [latex]1.0\times2^0=1[/latex]

Answer: B

questions.text:
Let [latex] T(n) [/latex] be the recurrence relation defined as follows:
[latex] \begin{aligned} & T(0)=1, \\ & T(1)=2, \text { and } \\ & T(n)=5 T(n-1)-6 T(n-2) \text { for } n \geq 2 \end{aligned} [/latex]
Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Characteristic equation: [latex]r^2-5r+6=0\Rightarrow r=2,3[/latex].
[latex]T(n)=\alpha2^n+\beta3^n[/latex]

[latex]T(0)=1:\ \alpha+\beta=1[/latex]
[latex]T(1)=2:\ 2\alpha+3\beta=2[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\beta=0,\ \alpha=1[/latex], so [latex]T(n)=2^n[/latex] (check: [latex]T(2)=10-6=4[/latex] True).

Answer: [latex]T(n)=\Theta(2^n)[/latex]
